answer: Mainly seasonal/humidity, not lot. Outdoor humidity jumps from ~50-55% (weeks 1-13) to 70-87% from week ~14. Residual metal rises with humidity above ~65% (~3 to 5-6 wt% at 90-100% RH) and oxidation onset falls (~590 C at 50-60% RH to ~550-565 C at 95%+). All lots follow the same humidity trend; lots FC-2606..2608 look worse (residual metal ~3.9-4.1 vs ~3.5; OT 575-578 vs 584) only because they were used in summer. Within each lot residual metal also rises over its weeks of use, but this is confounded with the humidity rise. Separate, non-seasonal issue: R4 runs ~1.2 wt% higher residual metal (4.7 vs ~3.4 for R1-R3) all year; R1-R3 rise from ~3.1 to ~3.7-4.4 in summer, R4 from ~4.4 to ~5. Not confirmed: causal proof (no stratified lot-by-humidity comparison), and OT by reactor not checked.
